author: blu
body: The CoAP client endpoint (RFC 7252): the binding that turns the Coap codec -- which only ever built and parsed packets -- into a request/response interaction with reliability. A constrained device asks a server for a resource and hears the answer, and if the datagram is lost it asks again.

author: blu
body: It is PURE, in the style of DtlsEndpoint and tcp-step: datagrams in, datagrams out, no socket and no clock. The transport `now` is a caller-supplied tick that drives retransmission, exactly the way the DTLS endpoint takes one. A thin os/net layer that carries the emitted datagrams over UDP (Udp + the NIC) is a separate wrapper; the reliability and correlation logic that was the actual missing piece lives here and is exercised by a loopback.

author: blu
body: A confirmable GET or POST. Refused with no output if an interaction is already in flight (NSTART = 1). The message id and token are assigned here and the datagram is kept, because a datagram that cannot be retransmitted is a request with no reliability at all.
